{{Short description|Type of linear representation of a group}}
{{inline |date=May 2024}}
In the [[mathematical]] fields of [[representation theory]] and [[group theory]], a [[linear representation]] <math>\rho</math> ([[rho]]) of a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] <math>G</math> is a '''monomial representation''' if there is a finite-index [[subgroup]] <math>H</math> and a one-dimensional linear representation <math>\sigma</math> of <math>H</math>, such that <math>\rho</math> is equivalent to the [[induced representation]] <math>\mathrm{Ind}_H^{G_\sigma}</math>.

Alternatively, one may define it as a representation whose [[Image (mathematics)|image]] is in the [[monomial matrices]].

Here for example <math>G</math> and <math>H</math> may be [[finite group]]s, so that ''induced representation'' has a classical sense. The monomial representation is only a little more complicated than the [[permutation representation]] of <math>G</math> on the [[coset]]s of <math>H</math>. It is necessary only to keep track of [[Scalar (mathematics)|scalar]]s coming from <math>\sigma</math> applied to elements of <math>H</math>.

== Definition ==
To define the monomial representation, we first need to introduce the notion of monomial space. A monomial space is a triple <math>(V,X,(V_x)_{x\in X})</math> where <math>V</math> is a finite-dimensional complex vector space, <math>X</math> is a finite set and <math>(V_x)_{x\in X}</math> is a family of one-dimensional subspaces of <math>V</math> such that <math>V=\oplus_{x\in X}V_x</math>.

Now Let <math>G</math> be a group, the monomial representation of <math>G</math> on <math>V</math> is a group homomorphism <math>\rho:G\to \mathrm{GL}(V)</math> such that for every element <math>g\in G</math>, <math>\rho(g)</math> permutes the <math>V_x</math>'s, this means that <math>\rho</math> induces an action by permutation of <math>G</math> on <math>X</math>.
